entry.content:
ROPPING Performance staged for camera, 2014.

Camera, Red one 4K, 7:28 minutes: by Rebeen and Rozhgar Mustafa

Alternativa 2014, Gdansk Poland

“Dropping” is a direct-to-camera performance recording by Rebeen Hamarafiq. Drops of milk fall at regular intervals onto the naked head of the artist filmed against a black background. Within a few minutes a small puddle of milk is formed on the top of the artist’s skull, and a thin trickle runs down his weary face. What we see is an obvious reference to the so-called Chinese water torture, in which cold water is slowly dripped onto the victim’s head. Seemingly mild and “humane”, deprived of spectacular violence and bloodshed, it is in reality painful, mentally debilitating and considered one of the most effective.

2014 Degree Show, Goldsmiths.

 

In the degree show at Goldsmiths, the work was shown with another work to build a space between swinging and looking at the video of the performance while the swing was 6 metres high; one was able to enjoy the dropping of the milk and build a space between enjoying swinging and watching the Chinese torture. The swings were made in my village, Delezha, by three old women as a collaborative work, encouraging them to build the biggest (guriss); the Kurdish name for the rope that the swing is made of. And while they had to make it very big, 14 metres long and four times thicker than normal ones-the work became work for many others to help them in the collaborative work they participated.

2020 Arsenal Gallery power station, ul. Elektryczna 13, Białystok

At Arsenal Gallery, Hamarafiq’s video is installed in a space below the level of the exhibition – the basement area symbolizing a torture chamber or prison, but also the humiliation of the victims of the abuse. The theme of torture often appears in the works of Kurdish artists, which has an obvious connection with the history of their nation and the painful experiences of their families and friends.
The motif of dripping milk also refers to Hamarafiq’s experience of fatherhood. The artist looked after his newborn daughter while his wife was working toward her university degree. Attempting to cope with a new situation, weary with the day-to-day monotony and challenges, the artist was also haunted by fear for his daughter’s future. It stemmed from, on the one hand, the artist’s memories of his own difficult childhood in Kurdistan under Saddam Hussein and, on the other, his desire to protect his daughter from experiencing Kurdish women’s sense of being unable to break through their limiting social, religious and cultural circumstances.

entry.content:
Photos of the head: Soran Salam

2005 Head’s back

The work combines fifteen prints in various tones but the same original photographs of my head; my effort was to rebuild the part we missed because of culture. At the time, there was a big positivity toward anything related to Kurdish culture, but in the work I was trying to look at culture critically.


Children in Kurdistan were tied up inside a cradle when they were born until they became older and could no longer stay in the cradle; in this process, the soft part at the child's head's back becomes pressed and flattened. This depressed part of the head metaphorically leaves a bigger depression in humans when they grow, as they are effortfully trying to rebuild their lost part.

The work was part of the 2005 Project exhibition; at the time, it was a new effort from our younger generation to discover working with other media and concepts outside painting.

entry.content:
Photo: Juli Adnan 2009

The work is a performance made in sulaymaniyeh City. In one of districkts which unplanned for expansion of the city happened, but the government didn’t provide services for those blocks. Beside Rebeen says that he had a problem with the back of his trousers getting muddy, something related to his way of walking; even though he tries hard to avoid it. 

On the day of the performance, he gets out from the home of Juli Adnan his friend, and walk for 17 minutes from home of his friend and goes back with his friend Juli Adnan who is also a profesional photographer taking a photo each minute of his trousers back.
